Select a 3D rendering backend

Source: R/coord-3d.R
backend_3d.Rd

Select a 3D rendering backend

Usage

backend_3d(
  type = "vector",
  dpi = 144,
  antialias = 2L,
  blend = "linear",
  samples = 64L,
  bounces = 8L,
  seed = 1L,
  aperture = 0,
  focus = NULL,
  light_radius = 5,
  progressive = FALSE,
  batch_size = 8L,
  geometry = "e3",
  observer = c(0, 0, 0),
  facing = diag(3),
  fov = 70,
  max_distance = 10,
  tolerance = 1e-05,
  max_steps = 2048L,
  quotient = NULL,
  light_size = 0.1,
  rasterise = "marked"
)

Arguments

type

Backend: "vector", "raster", "hybrid", "pathtrace", or "raymarch" (an intrinsic view in a Thurston geometry). A hybrid panel rasterises the layers created with raster = TRUE (an argument of every geom_*_3d() layer and of layer_3d()) into one image at dpi and draws the other layers, axes, panes and text as vector graphics. Vector geometry behind the image's opaque coverage is clipped at its pixels, so lines on or behind a rasterised surface stay exact where they are seen.

dpi

Physical raster resolution.

antialias

Positive integer supersampling factor.

blend

Colour space in which the raster backend composites translucent paint and averages antialiasing samples: "linear" light, encoded to sRGB after averaging, or "srgb", which matches the compositing of vector graphics devices.

samples

Path-tracing samples per pixel added by each render.

bounces

Maximum diffuse surface interactions per path.

seed

Nonnegative integer seed for pixel and sample indexed randomness.

aperture

Thin-lens radius in aspect-scaled model units; zero is a pinhole.

focus

Focal-plane distance along the camera forward axis, in model units. NULL focuses on the camera target.

light_radius

Angular radius of the distant light in degrees.

progressive

Accumulate samples across redraws of the same scene. Changes to geometry, camera, lighting or image dimensions reset accumulation.

batch_size

Samples per native batch; accumulation is independent of batch size and worker count. R can interrupt between batches.

geometry

Intrinsic geometry for the raymarch backend; see geodesic_3d().

observer

Observer coordinates in that geometry's chart.

facing

Orthonormal 3 by 3 matrix whose columns are the camera's right, up and forward tangent vectors in the observer's orthonormal frame.

fov

Vertical intrinsic field of view in degrees.

max_distance

Maximum intrinsic ray arc length.

tolerance

Surface residual and quotient-boundary tolerance.

max_steps

Maximum steps per intrinsic ray.

quotient

List of paired thurston_portal_3d() domain faces.

light_size

Positive point-light softening radius for intrinsic views.

rasterise

Layers a hybrid panel draws into its image: "marked", the layers created with raster = TRUE; "surfaces", which adds every depth-tested layer that draws faces or analytic quadrics; or "all", which adds every depth-tested layer with faces, paths or points. Text stays vector graphics, placed by the image's visibility.

Value

A backend configuration for coord_3d().

Details

The raster backend renders 64-pixel tiles in parallel. The number of worker threads is the option ggplot3d.threads; the default 0 uses one thread per hardware thread, at most two when _R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_ is set. The image does not depend on the thread count.

The native path tracer uses diffuse materials, a bounding-volume hierarchy, cosine-weighted reflection sampling and Russian roulette. The ambient light is a uniform environment; the diffuse light is a sampled distant disk. Points and paths use the solid conversion of export_3d(), and SDF layers use the shared sphere tracer. Furniture and text remain vector graphics.

The raymarch backend traces geodesics from an observer inside the geometry. Use geom_thurston_3d() for balls, cylinders and half-spaces, or traced SDF layers for chart-defined CSG. It draws a full-panel perspective image; Euclidean plot axes and exterior-camera settings have no intrinsic meaning. Lighting is an isotropic point light at the observer, with the ambient and diffuse strengths from light_3d(). Irradiance divides by the area density of geodesic spheres plus light_size^2. Each visible geodesic supplies its own light path, including paths through quotient faces. Intrinsic surfaces are opaque. See geodesic_3d() for charts and numerical accuracy details.

References

Pharr, Jakob and Humphreys (2023). Physically Based Rendering, fourth edition. https://pbr-book.org/4ed/Light_Transport_I_Surface_Reflection/Path_Tracing

Examples

backend_3d("vector")
backend_3d("raster", dpi = 144, antialias = 2)
backend_3d("raster", blend = "srgb")
backend_3d("pathtrace", samples = 8, seed = 1)
d <- expand.grid(x = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 40), y = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 40))
d$z <- sin(pi * d$x) * cos(pi * d$y)
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_surface_3d(fill = "grey80", colour = NA, raster = TRUE) +
  geom_contour_3d(colour = "black") +
  coord_3d(backend = backend_3d("hybrid", dpi = 150))
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_surface_3d(fill = "grey80", colour = NA) +
  coord_3d(backend = backend_3d("hybrid", dpi = 150, rasterise = "surfaces"))
